newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Frenchman denies compatriots held on Nigeria ship.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman denies compatriots held on Nigeria ship.

text.p: A Frenchman seaman on Monday said two compatriots reportedly held hostage by Nigerian workers on another vessel were actually visiting friends and not captives.

Twenty-eight foreigners held on a barge called the WB-82 for five days by workers demanding pay rises were freed by the Nigerian navy on Friday night and the captain of the barge then said that two Frenchmen were being held seperately on another ship, the American Pride.

"It is not correct to say they were held as hostages," Jean Lacombe, technical hook-up manager of the WB-82, told Reuters by telephone from a hotel in the southeastern town of Calabar where the freed foreigners were being lodged.
He said the two men had gone to another ship, American Pride, to see friends.
The Nigerians who took the 28 hostage were employed by NTPM, a French oil services company, on its barge WB-82 to transport crude oil from onshore fields to tankers.
